answer: No identity here is a haven for clones: standing requires eight epochs of passing, peer-graded work, renewed continuously. Like shale, each layer is thin alone, but stacked they bear weight; like cedar, growth cannot be rushed. A farm must pay that work and waiting cost for every single identity, in parallel, forever — so splitting into a thousand sybils multiplies the bill instead of diluting it, and going dormant lets the standing lapse.
